How To Read This

reflex-quant has the strongest relative profile in this run, 13.0% ahead of alien-signals by geometric mean. It takes 15 of 33 scenarios decisively, while alien-signals takes 3.

Each scenario was measured with all frameworks on one VM, on 3 independent VM sets, in 3 fresh processes per VM. The row score is the median of the per-machine estimates and its interval is their range; with 3 machines a range covers the cross-machine median with only ~75% probability, so it is not a 95% interval. The family-balanced leaderboard score is computed separately for each of the 3 machine sets (ratios within one VM) and the median is shown with the range; a ≈ next to a rank means the paired score ratios cross 1. Each workload group has equal weight in the overall score; the legacy flat score is also shown. With repeated estimates, ≈ and decisive wins use paired ratios on the same machine (or matched process rounds on one machine), rather than overlapping absolute time ranges. These descriptive ranges are not 95% confidence intervals. Single-process comparisons use median intervals. Censored rows record an invocation budget exceedance (cold for creation, post-warmup for steady workloads in protocol v3), not a median or its lower bound. Partial rows retain measured machines with their coverage. Neither censoring nor stress failures remove a framework from the core leaderboard; incomplete core scenarios are excluded for every participant. All intervals describe repeat measurements of this run, not the speed of a runtime on other hardware. Hover a row for its interval and noise.

Interpret wins through the scenario taxonomy: creation, update, pull/push propagation, dynamic dependency churn, large graphs, lifecycle pressure, and memory behavior can favor different runtimes.

Not ranked: dalien-signals (1 failed; 0 censored). Scoring incomplete measurements over only their completed scenarios would rank them on an easier workload set. Completed rows still appear in per-test cards.

Where The Noise Is

Spread of a row's medianTypical (median row)Rows
within one process±1.4%1420
between fresh processes±2.7%1420
between machines±18.8%1400
paired ratios between processes±4.1%1339
paired ratios between machines±4.6%1339

Each level is the standard deviation of ln(time), shown as an approximate relative spread, and includes the noise of the levels listed above it. The machine level compares per-machine estimates that are already medians over fresh processes, so it can be smaller than the process level. A within-process 95% interval only covers sample noise; in this run a fresh process or another machine typically moves a row 13.7x as much. Only the machine-level range reflects all three.

Paired spreads are SD of ln(time/reference time), using the same fully measured reference framework for each scenario. Processes pair by round within one VM; machines pair by machine round. Self-comparisons are excluded. These spreads are descriptive and help evaluate future sampling budgets.
